pairs: Hominis est animam præparare,
It is for man to prepare the soul,
et Domini gubernare linguam.
and for the Lord to govern the tongue.
Omnes viæ hominis patent oculis ejus;
All the ways of a man are open to his eyes;
spirituum ponderator est Dominus.
the Lord is the one who weighs spirits.
Revela Domino opera tua,
Open your works to the Lord,
et dirigentur cogitationes tuæ.
and your intentions will be set in order.
Universa propter semetipsum operatus est Dominus;
The Lord has wrought all things because of himself.
impium quoque ad diem malum.
Likewise the impious is for the evil day.
Abominatio Domini est omnis arrogans;
All the arrogant are an abomination to the Lord.
etiamsi manus ad manum fuerit,
Even if hand will be joined to hand,
non est innocens.
he is not innocent.
Initium viæ bonæ facere justitiam;
The beginning of a good way is to do justice.
accepta est autem apud Deum magis quam immolare hostias.
And this is more acceptable with God than to immolate sacrifices.
Misericordia et veritate redimitur iniquitas,
By mercy and truth, iniquity is redeemed.
et in timore Domini declinatur a malo.
And by the fear of the Lord, one turns away from evil.
Cum placuerint Domino viæ hominis,
When the ways of man will please the Lord,
inimicos quoque ejus convertet ad pacem.
he will convert even his enemies to peace.
Melius est parum cum justitia quam multi fructus cum iniquitate.
Better is a little with justice, than many fruits with iniquity.
Cor hominis disponit viam suam,
The heart of man disposes his way.
sed Domini est dirigere gressus ejus.
But it is for Lord to direct his steps.
Divinatio in labiis regis;
Foreknowledge is in the lips of the king.
in judicio non errabit os ejus.
His mouth shall not err in judgment.
Pondus et statera judicia Domini sunt,
Weights and scales are judgments of the Lord.
et opera ejus omnes lapides sacculi.
And all the stones in the bag are his work.
Abominabiles regi qui agunt impie,
Those who act impiously are abominable to the king.
quoniam justitia firmatur solium.
For the throne is made firm by justice.
Voluntas regum labia justa;
Just lips are the will of kings.
qui recta loquitur diligetur.
He who speaks honestly shall be loved.
Indignatio regis nuntii mortis,
The indignation of a king is a herald of death.
et vir sapiens placabit eam.
And the wise man will appease it.
In hilaritate vultus regis vita,
In the cheerfulness of the king’s countenance,
et clementia ejus quasi imber serotinus.
there is life. And his clemency is like belated rain.
Posside sapientiam,
Possess wisdom,
quia auro melior est,
for it is better than gold.
et acquire prudentiam,
And acquire prudence,
quia pretiosior est argento.
for it is more precious than silver.
Semita justorum declinat mala;
The path of the just turns away from evils.
custos animæ suæ servat viam suam.
He who guards his soul preserves his way.
Contritionem præcedit superbia,
Arrogance precedes destruction.
et ante ruinam exaltatur spiritus.
And the spirit is exalted before a fall.
Melius est humiliari cum mitibus quam dividere spolia cum superbis.
It is better to be humbled with the meek, than to divide spoils with the arrogant.
Eruditus in verbo reperiet bona,
The learned in word shall find good things.
et qui sperat in Domino beatus est.
And whoever hopes in the Lord is blessed.
Qui sapiens est corde appellabitur prudens,
Whoever is wise in heart shall be called prudent.
et qui dulcis eloquio majora percipiet.
And whoever is sweet in eloquence shall attain to what is greater.
Fons vitæ eruditio possidentis;
Learning is a fountain of life to one who possesses it.
doctrina stultorum fatuitas.
The doctrine of the foolish is senseless.
Cor sapientis erudiet os ejus,
The heart of the wise shall instruct his mouth
et labiis ejus addet gratiam.
and add grace to his lips.
Favus mellis composita verba;
Careful words are a honeycomb:
dulcedo animæ sanitas ossium.
sweet to the soul and healthful to the bones.
Est via quæ videtur homini recta,
There is a way which seems right to a man,
et novissima ejus ducunt ad mortem.
and its end result leads to death.
Anima laborantis laborat sibi,
The soul of the laborer labors for himself,
quia compulit eum os suum.
because his mouth has driven him to it.
Vir impius fodit malum,
The impious man digs up evil,
et in labiis ejus ignis ardescit.
and in his lips is a burning fire.
Homo perversus suscitat lites,
A perverse man stirs up lawsuits.
et verbosus separat principes.
And one who is verbose divides leaders.
Vir iniquus lactat amicum suum,
A man of iniquity entices his friend,
et ducit eum per viam non bonam.
and he leads him along a way that is not good.
Qui attonitis oculis cogitat prava,
Whoever, with astonished eyes, thinks up depravities,
mordens labia sua perficit malum.
biting his lips, accomplishes evil.
Corona dignitatis senectus,
Old age is a crown of dignity,
quæ in viis justitiæ reperietur.
when it is found in the ways of justice.
Melior est patiens viro forti,
A patient man is better than a strong one.
et qui dominatur animo suo expugnatore urbium.
And whoever rules his soul is better than one who assaults cities.
Sortes mittuntur in sinum,
Lots are cast into the lap,
sed a Domino temperantur.
but they are tempered by the Lord.
